screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic classification analysis of ASD vs TC using resting-state fMRI connectivity from ABIDE with the CC200 atlas (Inclusion 2, 3)

evidence_spans.text:
With cross-validation strategy, our proposed method resulted in a mean classification ac-
curacy of 72.2% (sensitivity=68.6%, specificity=75.4%).
evidence_spans.claim: Proposed Extra-Trees attention + SVM method achieved 72.2% accuracy (sensitivity 68.6%, specificity 75.4%) classifying ASD vs TC.

evidence_spans.text:
We successfully downloaded a dataset 
of 1102 subjects from the Preprocessed Connectomes Project, 
and then excluded subjects whose imaging data shows some miss-
ing. Finally, data of 506 ASD individuals and 548 controls was 
included in our study.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was 506 ASD and 548 control subjects retained after excluding subjects with missing imaging data from the 1102-subject ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project download.

evidence_spans.text:
There was no difference in the age, sex and FD between 
cases and controls (p>0.05).
evidence_spans.claim: Age, sex and mean framewise displacement did not differ significantly between ASD and control groups.

evidence_spans.text:
The rs-fMRI data utilized in this study was preprocessed with 
the Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Conenectomes (C-
PAC). The preprocessing procedure covers the operation of slice 
time and motion corrected, as well as voxel intensity normalized.
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed with the C-PAC pipeline (slice timing, motion correction, intensity normalization, nuisance regression, band-pass filtering, ANTs normalization to MNI152).

evidence_spans.text:
Finally, the 1935 top features were selected to 
perform the differentiation between individuals with ASD and TC 
via the SVM classifier. 
To ensure the reliability of experimental result, we utilized 10-
fold cross-validation to measure the accuracy of predicted label.
evidence_spans.claim: Feature selection (top 1935 connectivity features via Extra-Trees attention) is described before the 10-fold cross-validation step, with only hyper-parameters set via nested cross-validation.

evidence_spans.text:
For the challenges of site-related 
variability, we also performed an intra-site prediction based on the 
stratified shuffle split cross-validation.
evidence_spans.claim: Site-related variability was examined via an intra-site stratified shuffle-split cross-validation in addition to the pooled 10-fold CV.

evidence_spans.text:
Inte-
grated simulation results revealed that the mean score on accuracy, 
sensitivity, and specificity are 72.2%, 68.8%, and 75.4% respectively.

For the intra-site cross validation, the 
highest accuracy resulted in 71.2%, and the mean classification 
accuracy was 67.7% (sensitivity=66.3%, specificity=68.9%) with a 
range of accuracy of 64.0% to 71.2% in individual folds.
evidence_spans.claim: Intra-site cross-validation gave a mean accuracy of 67.7% (range 64.0-71.2% across folds), somewhat lower than the pooled 10-fold result.

evidence_spans.text:
manifested lower correlation between the anterior and posterior default mode network (DMN) in autis-
tic individuals than controls.
evidence_spans.claim: Autistic individuals showed lower (hypo-) correlation between anterior and posterior DMN than controls.

assessments.support: N by diagnosis (506 ASD/548 TC) and site count (17) reported, but the only exclusion rule stated is "excluded subjects whose imaging data shows some missing" with no motion/QC threshold.
C-PAC pipeline with nuisance regression, band-pass filtering and ANTs normalization is described, and CC200 atlas connectivity is the feature basis.
ASD vs TC labels used without stating the diagnostic instrument/source.

The top 1935 features are described as selected before the 10-fold CV procedure is introduced, suggesting feature selection may not have been confined to training folds; the pooled 10-fold CV does not account for site, though a separate intra-site stratified shuffle-split analysis was also run (lower accuracy, 67.7%, suggesting some site-driven inflation in the pooled result).

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort size, sites and pipeline (C-PAC, CC200) are well reported, but the exclusion rule is minimal (missing data only, no motion threshold), diagnosis source is not stated, and the description of feature selection preceding cross-validation raises a leakage concern; a supplementary intra-site evaluation showed lower accuracy than the pooled 10-fold result, consistent with some site leakage in the main result.

charting.title: Attentional Connectivity-based Prediction of Autism Using Heterogeneous rs-fMRI Data from CC200 Atlas
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) vs Typical Control (TC)
charting.age_matched: No significant difference in age between groups (p>0.05)
charting.specific_features: Pairwise functional connectivity from CC200 atlas ROIs; top 1935 connectivity features selected via an Extra-Trees attention mechanism
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC); CC200 atlas (Preprocessed Connectomes Project)
charting.importance_method: Extra-Trees-based attention mechanism (feature importance/attention vector over connectivity features)
charting.top_features_identified: Connections involving regions implicated in social cognition and interaction; anterior-posterior default mode network (DMN) connections
charting.feature_change_direction: Lower correlation between anterior and posterior DMN in autistic individuals than controls
charting.specific_algorithms: Extra-Trees attention mechanism for feature selection, linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier
charting.validation_methodology: 10-fold cross-validation (hyperparameters set via nested cross-validation), plus a supplementary intra-site stratified shuffle-split cross-validation (80/20 train/test) to examine site effects
charting.key_performance_results: Pooled 10-fold CV: accuracy 72.2%, sensitivity 68.6-68.8%, specificity 75.4%; intra-site stratified shuffle-split CV: mean accuracy 67.7% (range 64.0-71.2%), sensitivity 66.3%, specificity 68.9%
charting.summary_key_findings: An Extra-Trees attention mechanism combined with a linear SVM classified ASD vs TC from ABIDE rs-fMRI CC200 connectivity with 72.2% accuracy (68.6% sensitivity, 75.4% specificity) in pooled 10-fold CV, exceeding prior comparable work by about 2% precision and 3.2% specificity; informative connections involved social-cognition regions and showed reduced anterior-posterior DMN correlation in autism; accuracy dropped to 67.7% under an intra-site evaluation.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs TC); ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project release (ABIDE I), 506 ASD/548 TC across 17 sites
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with the CC200 atlas; an Extra-Trees attention mechanism selected the top 1935 connectivity features, classified with a linear SVM; evaluated with pooled 10-fold cross-validation (nested CV for hyperparameters) and a supplementary intra-site stratified shuffle-split cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: 72.2% accuracy (68.6-68.8% sensitivity, 75.4% specificity) in pooled 10-fold CV, versus 67.7% mean accuracy (66.3% sensitivity, 68.9% specificity) under the intra-site evaluation; informative connections implicated social-cognition regions and reduced anterior-posterior DMN correlation in autism.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Exclusion rule limited to missing imaging data with no motion/QC threshold; diagnosis source not reported; feature selection appears to precede the cross-validation split, raising a leakage concern; pooled-CV accuracy exceeds the site-stratified accuracy, consistent with some site leakage.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A CC200/C-PAC predictive study with a clearly reported N and pipeline but an apparent feature-selection leakage gap and only a partial (non-leave-site-out) site-handling check.
